verdict_label: Not taboo, but keep it tidy
explanation: Spain has no cultural taboo against showing the soles of your feet the way Thailand or Gulf countries do — there's no belief that feet are spiritually 'low' or impure. That said, Spaniards are particular about feet generally: going barefoot indoors, even in someone's own home, is seen as a bit odd, and propping feet up on furniture in someone's house still comes across as overly casual.
local_tip: Don't worry about which way your feet point, but keep your shoes or slippers on and your feet off the furniture when visiting someone's home.

also_check.note: Feet are considered the lowest, most impure part of the body, so pointing soles at a person, a monk, or a Buddha image is genuinely offensive.
There's no strong taboo, but propping feet on furniture or a table in someone's home can read as disrespectful or overly casual.
Feet are considered unclean, so showing the soles of your shoes to someone, especially elders, is seen as insulting.

sources.title: 13 things foreigners do that make Spaniards feel really awkward
